Independent review (Claude Sonnet 5, read-only, local hash/file inspection, no execution) of the supplemental packet in docs/rewrite-agents/tasks/CACHE_VALIDATORS_20261013 (prepared.json, reviewed-prepare.sh, reviewed-publication.sh, prepare.log, regression.json, source-review.json, feedback-inventory.json) plus committed source d851284 and next/infra/production/*.

Verified myself: nginx.conf locally re-hashes to e9add812... matching prepared/regression 'fixed' config_sha256, LF-only; diff from the prior published config is exactly one comment + `etag off;`/`if_modified_since off;`, all routes/headers/limits untouched. reviewed-publication.sh re-hashes to c1989c29... (matches prepared.json publish_script_sha256); prepare.log re-hashes to 537a8298... (matches prepare_log_sha256); prepare.log's embedded JSON is byte-identical to prepared.json -- evidence is self-consistent, not substituted. Commit d851284 contains exactly the claimed canonical nginx.conf/Dockerfile/regression; the new prepared.json/scripts/feedback-inventory.json are untracked, consistent with 'prepared but not published'. source-review.json confirms task-3bad1bb3... (config copy) was independently ACCEPTED in the prior gate by a different Claude session.

Scripts: both guard exact hostname and flock the same lockfile (mutually exclusive fds 8/9); pin baseline image digest/PVC UID/Helm rev 46/disk/node readiness; verify base image ID unchanged before and after `docker build --network=none --pull=false` with explicit --build-arg (InvalidDefaultArgInFrom warning is expected/benign, caller supplies and verifies BASE_IMAGE); cmp all API/Web file hashes baseline vs candidate; extract+diff built image's live nginx.conf vs source; guard archive overwrite/symlinked image dir; validate imported digest format; assert rendered baseline vs candidate manifests differ in exactly the two image references (programmatic assert). Publication script re-verifies all hashes + durable-image.sha256, re-renders and cmp's against the already-reviewed rendered.yaml, takes a read-only sqlite3 URI backup with integrity_check (no restore), runs `helm upgrade --atomic --wait`. Its ERR trap only rolls back to rev 46 when post-upgrade state is exactly candidate-image@rev47; any other mismatch is left alone with a warning rather than guessed-at -- sound conservative precondition, correctly never restores the DB. Post-publish checks compare live bytes/headers at the real domain against previously checksummed prior-release files and resynthesize the old ETag scheme to prove stale validators no longer 304, directly targeting the regression.

Limits (as disclosed): proves a correctly prepared, self-consistent execution gate, not that publication occurred (Helm still at rev 46/baseline image). TOCTOU window between base-image recheck and save/import is nonzero but mitigated by flock/single-operator assumption. No live /v1/ proxy check post-publish beyond config diff (in scope since those locations are provably untouched). No syntax/hash/control-flow bugs found in either script.

Verdict: accept -- approves this prepared execution gate as sound and ready; does not certify publication already happened.

review_text:
Review recorded as **ACCEPT** for task-1d3c57e523074692953b8e4c38c74714 in the hub (state now `ACCEPTED`).

Summary of findings:
- Verified the evidence myself (hashes, diffs, commit contents), not just the claims: `nginx.conf` locally re-hashes to `e9add812...` matching `prepared.json`/`regression.json`; `reviewed-publication.sh` and `prepare.log` locally re-hash to the exact values recorded inside `prepared.json`, so the evidence packet is self-consistent and not substituted.
- The config diff is exactly one comment + `etag off;`/`if_modified_since off;`, nothing else touched.
- Both scripts are well-guarded: hostname pin, mutual-exclusion flock, pre/post base-image-ID checks around the build, byte-for-byte app-file hash comparisons, exact-diff assertions on rendered Helm manifests (only the two image refs differ), read-only SQLite backup with integrity check and no DB restore, and a conservative rollback trap that only fires on an unambiguous candidate@rev47 state (otherwise it preserves state rather than guessing).
- No syntax, hash-mismatch, or control-flow problems found. The `InvalidDefaultArgInFrom` Docker warning is expected/benign given the caller supplies and verifies `BASE_IMAGE`.
- This accept approves the prepared execution gate as sound and ready — it does **not** certify that publication has actually happened (Helm is still at baseline revision 46).

No edits, builds, or deployment actions were performed; this was a read-only review as scoped.
